images.title: Counting fourth pieces
images.purpose: Set up the question: draw and write 5 × 1/4 and 9 × 1/4 of a roti, using the fact that 4 fourth pieces make 1 roti.
images.composition: Three groups in one row with wide gaps: one whole roti in fourths, a small group of five loose pieces, and a square group of nine loose pieces.
images.exact_structure: Left: one round roti cut by two straight lines through the centre into 4 equal pieces, outlined grey #6B7280, plain. Middle: 5 loose fourth pieces of exactly that size, filled teal #0072B2, in one row. Right: 9 loose fourth pieces of exactly that size, filled amber #E69F00, in 3 rows of 3. No pieces joined into rotis. Exactly 1 roti, 5 teal pieces, 9 amber pieces.

images.takeaway: 4 fourths make 1 roti, so count the fourths and group them into rotis.
images.description: A roti cut into 4 equal pieces marked 4 × 1/4 = 1 roti, beside 5 loose teal fourth pieces and 9 loose amber fourth pieces, each group with a question.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say how many full rotis the loose pieces in each group can make.

image_decisions.why: A roti in fourths beside the loose pieces cues grouping four at a time while leaving both answers to the student.
